title: Honey Roast Parsnips
subtitle: Caramelised parsnips with honey and thyme
excerpt: Parsnip pieces roasted in a hot oven until the edges are caramelised, then finished with honey and thyme for a sticky, golden glaze. The classic British roast dinner side.

recipe.sourceNotes: Honey roast parsnips are a fixture of the British Sunday roast, particularly from autumn through to spring when parsnips are in season. Parsnips were a staple British vegetable long before potatoes arrived from the Americas. The honey glaze is added near the end of roasting rather than the beginning: added too early it burns before the parsnip is cooked through. Choose medium parsnips; very large ones can be woody at the core.

recipeTools.notes: Large enough so the parsnips are in a single layer.

content.text: The oven must be properly hot before the parsnips go in: if the tin goes into a cold oven the parsnips steam rather than roast. Leave space between the pieces; crowding traps moisture and prevents browning. Add the honey only in the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Place a large roasting tin in the oven while it heats up.

Toss the parsnip batons with the oil, salt, and pepper. Carefully pour them into the hot tin in a single layer. Tuck in the thyme sprigs. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once halfway, until the parsnips are golden and tender.
Drizzle the honey over the parsnips. Turn to coat. Roast for a further 8 to 10 minutes until the edges are deep golden and sticky. Serve immediately.
